title: The operator sees an environment go down and rolls it back from the incident card
description:
SPIDR child 3 of task-7683a432eb3f4e87b1eb0cbc6e3a55ff (architect-20a6d1eb, 2026-09-05). dependsOn child 1 (task-6ec875f4dd5f4f2ab97e46f71bf57b2b, the probe and the incident) and child 2 (task-95e68a8dd2464e7b8ad4b1f8c4d2b2e4, the backups and the rollback). PROOF ROW: owns the UI, the Playwright journey, the live drive and the docs (global rail 21).

WHAT THIS ROW OWNS: the Deployments card showing UP / DEGRADED / DOWN with the last probe and a latency sparkline (last hour); the backups list with its restore-proof state; a Rollback arm/confirm; the Needs-you INCIDENT card ('production unhealthy since <t>: roll back to <prev sha>?' with the last error line) offering Roll back / Dismiss; and an 'Environments' section on the Health screen.

THIS IS AN INCIDENT SURFACE, so it is read by someone under time pressure who will act on it. Three consequences: the last ERROR LINE must be shown verbatim (an operator diagnosing an outage needs the actual error, not 'unhealthy'); the sha being rolled back TO must be named on the confirm, since rolling back to the wrong one during an incident is a second incident; and DISMISS must be distinguishable from RESOLVED - dismissing a card while the environment is still down must not make it look recovered.

THE BACKUPS LIST SHOWS RESTORE-PROOF STATE, not just existence. Child 2 records a restore-to-temp sha256 per backup; a list that shows only 'backup taken' would hide exactly the distinction that row exists to establish.

MEASURED AT HEAD (branch moe/work-2026-09-04) by architect-20a6d1eb: the Health screen is at apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/ops-screens.tsx (228 lines, close to the 250 ceiling - a new Environments section likely belongs in its own module); Needs-you is needs-you-model.ts (NEEDS_YOU_KINDS at :28) plus needs-you.tsx, both being extended concurrently by task-a988ca1c, task-33ceae56 and task-84cd2e55 - expect a rebase. The ops reads are wired in live-ops.tsx and every live read client decodes EXACT-KEY.
definitionOfDone: The Deployments card shows UP / DEGRADED / DOWN with the last probe time and a latency sparkline over the last hour, driven by child 1's ring from a REAL daemon frame.

The Needs-you INCIDENT card renders 'production unhealthy since <t>' with THE LAST ERROR LINE VERBATIM and offers Roll back / Dismiss. Assert the error text reaches the card - an operator diagnosing an outage needs the actual error, and 'unhealthy' sends them to the logs the card was supposed to replace.
THE ROLLBACK CONFIRM NAMES THE TARGET SHA. Assert the sha being rolled back to is shown at the moment of confirmation; during an incident, rolling back to the wrong sha is a second incident.

DISMISS IS NOT RESOLVE: dismissing an incident card while the environment is still DOWN leaves the environment visibly DOWN elsewhere, and the card returns on the next failure threshold rather than staying silent. Assert both - a dismiss that reads as recovery is how an outage gets forgotten.
The backups list shows each backup's RESTORE-PROOF state (proven / failed / not yet checked), not merely that a backup exists - that distinction is what child 2 exists to establish.
The Health screen gains an 'Environments' section; a Playwright journey against a REAL daemon covers DOWN -> incident card -> rollback -> recovery, with the `pnpm test:e2e:browser` count line quoted.

LIVE DRIVE: a deployed PREVIEW environment probed for at least 10 minutes, a FORCED failure raising the incident card, and a rollback restoring the previous sha - a probe-ring excerpt and the receipts in a row comment under ~4500 chars. If no environment is deployed (the deployment row is a sibling that may not have landed), record that plainly rather than simulating it. Runbook + README updated; gates quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm test:e2e:browser`.
taskRails: THIS IS AN INCIDENT SURFACE. It is read under time pressure: show the real error line, name the target sha on the confirm, and never let Dismiss read as recovery.
THIS ROW PROVES, IT DOES NOT REBUILD: a probe or incident-raising defect is child 1's, a backup or rollback defect is child 2's. Comment there and report_blocked.
SHOW RESTORE-PROOF STATE, not backup existence. The distinction is the whole point of child 2's restore check.

needs-you-model.ts and ops-screens.tsx are being edited by three other rows concurrently - rebase, do not delete a peer's entry; ops-screens.tsx is 228 lines against a 250 ceiling, so put the Environments section in its own module.
ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (scheduler package-boundary scan); check any new testid namespace is free; EXACT-KEY decoders plus a dev-proxy-paths pin for any new read.

implementationPlan.description:
CONFIRM THE FOUR PROPERTIES THAT MAKE THIS AN INCIDENT SURFACE RATHER THAN A DASHBOARD. Check the ASSERTION SHAPE, not merely that an arm exists — each of these has a way of passing while being wrong.

(a) THE REAL ERROR LINE (B's DoD 1). Confirm the arm asserts the EXACT error text reaches the card, not that some error-ish string is present. A card rendering only "unhealthy" sends the operator to the logs it was built to replace.

(b) THE CONFIRM NAMES THE SHA (B's DoD 2). Confirm the assertion is on the CONFIRM surface, not the card behind it. The confirm is the moment the operator commits, and rolling back to the wrong sha during an incident is a second incident.

(c) DISMISS IS NOT RESOLVE (B's DoD 3). Confirm BOTH directions are asserted: still DOWN on the Environments surface after a dismiss, AND the card returns at the next failure threshold. One direction alone permits a dismiss that quietly ends monitoring — which is how an outage gets forgotten.

(d) RESTORE-PROOF STATE IN THREE VALUES (A's DoD 3). Confirm "not yet checked" is asserted as NOT rendering as proven. Collapsing those two is the exact distinction the restore check exists to establish, and an operator leans on it at the worst possible moment.

Then confirm the two structural properties that keep the browser honest:
  - The card renders the state the DAEMON derived and does not recompute UP/DEGRADED/DOWN client-side (A's DoD 2). A browser-side derivation is a second opinion about one ring.
  - The Roll back control is OFFERED BY THE DAEMON, absent when no rollback is offered (B's DoD 5). A browser-minted control can offer what the command path refuses — the dead-button hazard this board has already shipped once.

SECOND-SOURCED STEP-2 VERIFICATION, from the YIELDING twin session (03:04-03:12Z, 2026-09-08, seat worker-4d8571e7). TWO seats hold this row: claude.exe PID 57132 (launched 03:01:24Z, mcp-config worker-60888) and PID 45440 (03:01:33Z, worker-71748). step-1 closed 03:03:50.853Z by a call I never made and step-2 opened 03:03:56.527Z, so the OTHER session is driving. I made no complete_step, no writes, no status change. This is read-only corroboration so step 2's conclusion is not single-sourced. Measured at HEAD 464481ef.

ALL SIX PROPERTIES CONFIRMED, and four are stronger than the step asked for.

(a) THE REAL ERROR LINE - CONFIRMED, exact not error-ish. incident-card.test.tsx:58 `card.textContent).toContain(ERROR_LINE)` over the WHOLE rendered container PLUS :59 `getByTestId(...error).textContent).toBe(ERROR_LINE)` - toBe, not toContain, on the dedicated node. Three arms beyond the ask: :62 a 480+ char line asserted `toBe(line)` and `not.toContain("...")`, so no truncation or ellipsis; :78 the refusal code+layer asserted BESIDE the line in `.errormeta` and asserted `not.toContain("DEPLOY_HEALTHCHECK_FAILED")` INSIDE `.error`, which is what stops the line degrading into a summary; :90 SINCE comes from the incident openedAt and `not.toContain(LAST_PROBE_AT)`. Fixtures arrive through `deriveNeedsYou` over a health frame decoded by the production client and render through the WHOLE `NeedsYou` queue, not the leaf - a leaf-only test would stay green the day the queue stopped rendering the card.

(b) THE CONFIRM NAMES THE SHA - CONFIRMED, on the confirm surface. :130 asserts `.confirm` is NULL before arming, so the surface asserted at :136 exists only once armed. The sha compared is `TARGET_SHA` from the read's own `rollbackTarget.sha`, never a hex pattern. Also on the armed button text and its aria-label (:141). BEYOND THE ASK, and this is the sharpest thing in the file: a two-environments-down describe (:180+) proves each card carries its OWN sha at the confirm - arming staging shows STAGING_SHA and `not.toContain(TARGET_SHA)`, production's confirm stays null and its button still reads "Roll back". The offer is minted once per project, so `rollbackTarget` is the only per-environment authority; had the queue keyed on `goalId` (which is "" by design for an incident) React would reuse one card and the two would share the armed confirm - arm staging, read production's sha, confirm. That is DoD 3's own hazard as a reconciliation bug, and no single-environment fixture can see it.

(c) DISMISS IS NOT RESOLVE - CONFIRMED, BOTH directions, in incident-dismiss.test.tsx. Direction 1 (:126) renders the REAL `EnvironmentsSection` from the SAME decoded outcome object the queue held: `data-status` toBe "DOWN", the word "Down", and "Incident 7" still open there. Direction 2 (:162) advances the feed to UP/incident null, asserts the card stays gone, then to a NEW incident id 8 and asserts the card RETURNS as `cr.needsyou.item.incident.production#8` while `production#7` stays dismissed - a dismissal, not a reset. :183 asserts the card's own note says "stays down" and "next failure threshold".
THE VACUITY HAZARD IS EXPLICITLY CLOSED, which is the thing worth reporting. Direction 1 leans on `expect(sendCommand).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`.
